title: Source widths inferred from the 2023 ASASSN-14ko X-ray ingress depend on the flicker model
abstract: We jointly fit 57 XMM-Newton bins in each of two disjoint energy bands during the 2023 ASASSN-14ko ingress. In a straight opaque-edge model, the ingress width ratio equals the projected Gaussian source width ratio. Fully shared fractional flicker gives a hard/soft width ratio near 0.87 and an equal-width cost of 13.31 in twice log likelihood. Fitting the band correlation, amplitudes and time scale lowers the cost to 4.37. A model with fast common flicker and independent 0.2-day band fluctuations gives a cost of 0.64. The fitted one-scale family has a nominal AIC advantage of 5.05 over that two-scale free fit, so the families are not equally supported. The small inferred size difference is sensitive to the covariance model. These conditional fit costs are not calibrated probabilities. The result limits eclipse mapping from one grey ingress; it does not establish an opaque screen, an intrinsic switch-off or a stellar orbital period. Original code, aggregate profiles, numerical checks and verified source retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Joint hard/soft projected width profiles and the cost of equal widths under several flicker models. The 3.84 reference is not a calibrated confidence limit.
